workflow.name: Publish RSS articles to LinkedIn and Instagram using OpenAI and Gemini images
workflow.description:
This n8n workflow automatically converts new RSS feed articles into ready-to-publish social media posts for LinkedIn and Instagram.

Whenever a new article is detected from the RSS feed, the workflow extracts the article title, link, description, and publish date. It then uses OpenAI to generate a professional LinkedIn post, a short Instagram caption, relevant hashtags, and an image prompt. After that, Google Gemini generates a custom image, UploadToURL converts the generated image into a public image URL, and the workflow publishes the final content to LinkedIn and Instagram.

---

## What This Workflow Does

- Watches an RSS feed for new articles
- Extracts article title, link, description, and publish date
- Uses OpenAI to generate LinkedIn and Instagram content
- Creates an AI-generated image using Google Gemini
- Uploads the generated image to a public URL using UploadToURL
- Publishes the AI-generated post to LinkedIn
- Publishes the generated image and caption to Instagram

---

# Node-by-Node Explanation

---

## 1. Watch RSS Feed for New Articles

### What this node does

This node monitors an RSS feed and checks for new articles every hour.

### How it works

The RSS Feed Trigger runs automatically based on the configured polling schedule. In this workflow, it checks the RSS feed every hour.

When a new article is found, the node outputs article data such as:

- Title
- Link
- Publish date
- Description
- Content snippet

### Why it is important

This node starts the automation. Instead of manually checking a blog, news website, or company update page, the workflow automatically detects fresh content and begins the social media publishing process.

---

## 2. Extract Article Data

### What this node does

This node cleans and organizes the raw RSS feed data into simple fields that can be used in the next steps.

### How it works

It extracts the important article details and stores them in clean fields:

- `article_title`
- `article_link`
- `article_description`
- `published_date`

---

## 3. Generate Social Media Content

### What this node does

This node uses AI to create platform-ready social media content from the RSS article.

### How it works

It sends the article title, description, and link to the OpenAI model and asks it to return valid JSON only.

The generated JSON includes:

- `content_angle`
- `linkedin_post`
- `instagram_caption`
- `instagram_image_prompt`
- `hashtags`
---

## 4. Parse AI JSON Output

### What this node does

This node converts the AI-generated JSON text into clean structured fields.

### How it works

Sometimes AI returns JSON inside markdown code blocks. This node first removes unwanted formatting like:

```text
```json
```
```

Then it parses the cleaned text using:

```js
JSON.parse()
```

After parsing, it returns these fields:

- `content_angle`
- `linkedin_post`
- `instagram_caption`
- `instagram_image_prompt`
- `hashtags`
- `hashtags_text`

### Why it is important

The next nodes need structured data, not raw AI text. This node makes sure the AI output becomes proper fields that can be used by the image generation, LinkedIn, and Instagram nodes.

### Error handling

If the AI output is not valid JSON, this node throws an error. This helps catch formatting issues before the workflow publishes anything.

---

## 5. Generate an Image

### What this node does

This node generates an AI image for the social media post.

### How it works

It uses Google Gemini image generation with the model:

```text
models/gemini-2.5-flash-image
```

The image prompt comes from the parsed AI output:

```js
$json.instagram_image_prompt
```

The prompt describes the visual concept, style, and layout for the image.

### Why it is important

This node creates a custom visual automatically, so the workflow can publish image-based posts instead of only text updates.

---

## 6. Upload a File

### What this node does

This node uploads the AI-generated image and converts it into a public image URL using **UploadToURL**.

### How it works

After the image is generated by Google Gemini, the file is passed to the **Upload a File** node.  
UploadToURL receives the generated image file, uploads it, and returns a publicly accessible CDN URL.

That public URL is then used by the Instagram node to publish the generated image.

### Why it is important

Many social media platforms and APIs require a public image URL before they can publish media.  
This node solves that problem by converting the generated image file into a shareable public link automatically.
[UploadToURL](https://uploadtourl.com/)

---

## 7. Publish LinkedIn Post

### What this node does

This node publishes the AI-generated LinkedIn post.

### How it works

It takes the LinkedIn post text from the **Parse AI JSON Output** node:

```js
$('Parse AI JSON Output').item.json.linkedin_post
```

The LinkedIn node is configured to publish a post using the generated content.

---

## 8. Publish Instagram Post

### What this node does

This node publishes the generated image and caption to Instagram.

### How it works

It uses the public image URL returned from the UploadToURL node:

```js
$json.url
```

It also uses the Instagram caption generated by AI:

```js
$('Parse AI JSON Output').item.json.instagram_caption
```

### Why it is important

This node completes the Instagram publishing process by posting both the generated image and the AI-written caption automatically.

nodes.name: Watch RSS Feed for New Articles

parameters.text:
=You are a social media strategist.

Create platform-ready social media content from this RSS article.

Article Title:
{{$json.article_title}}

Article Description:
{{$json.article_description}}

Article Link:
{{$json.article_link}}

Generate the output in valid JSON only.

Rules:
- LinkedIn post should be professional, insightful, and include the article link.
- Instagram caption should be short, engaging, and include hashtags.
- Instagram image prompt should describe a clean, modern, scroll-stopping visual.
- Do not use markdown.
- Do not add fake facts.
- Keep the tone clear and human.

- Do not mention "we", "our", or "us" unless the article is from our own company.
- LinkedIn post should be under 900 characters.
- Instagram caption should be under 300 characters.
- Hashtags should be relevant and maximum 5.
- Do not generate fake statistics.
- Avoid copyrighted logo descriptions unless the article clearly mentions the brands.
- Return valid JSON only, no explanation.

Return this exact JSON structure:

{
  "content_angle": "",
  "linkedin_post": "",
  "instagram_caption": "",
  "instagram_image_prompt": "",
  "hashtags": []
}

## Step 1: Watch RSS Feed for New Articles

### What this node does
This node monitors an RSS feed and checks for new articles every hour.

### How it works
Whenever a new item appears in the RSS feed, this node triggers the workflow automatically.  
It receives article data such as the title, link, publish date, content snippet, and description from the RSS feed.

## Step 2: Extract Article Data

### What this node does
This node cleans and organizes the raw RSS feed data into simple fields that can be used in the next steps.

### How it works
It extracts the main article information from the RSS output:

- article_title
- article_link
- article_description
- published_date

## Step 3: Generate Social Media Content

### What this node does
This node uses AI to create social media content from the RSS article.

### How it works
It sends the article title, description, and link to the AI model and asks it to generate structured JSON output containing:

- content_angle
- linkedin_post
- instagram_caption
- instagram_image_prompt
- hashtags

## Step 4: Parse AI JSON Output

### What this node does
This node converts the AI-generated JSON text into clean workflow fields.

### Why it is important
AI sometimes returns JSON as plain text.  
This node makes sure the output becomes proper structured data that can be used by the image generation, LinkedIn, and Instagram nodes.

## Step 5: Generate an Image

### What this node does
This node generates an image for the social media post.

### How it works
It uses Google Gemini image generation and takes the `instagram_image_prompt` created by the AI content node.  
The prompt describes the visual style, layout, and concept for the image.

# Step 7: Upload a File

### What this node does
This node uploads the generated image and converts it into a public image URL.

### How it works
The image generated by Gemini is passed as a file/binary output to this node.  
UploadToURL uploads the image and returns a public CDN URL.

### Why it is important
Instagram and many social platforms require a public image URL for posting.  
This node solves that problem by converting the generated image file into a shareable hosted URL.

## Step 6: Publish LinkedIn Post with Image

### What this node does
This node publishes the AI-generated LinkedIn post along with the generated image.

### How it works
It takes the LinkedIn post text from the **Parse AI JSON Output** node:

## Node 8: Publish Instagram Post

### What this node does
This node publishes the generated image and caption to Instagram.

### How it works
It takes the public image URL from the UploadToURL node and uses the AI-generated Instagram caption from the parsed AI output.

# Workflow Overview

### This workflow automatically monitors an RSS feed for new articles and converts each article into ready-to-publish social media content.  
### It extracts the article title, link, description, and publish date, then uses AI to generate a LinkedIn post, Instagram caption, hashtags, and an image prompt.  
### The workflow creates an AI-generated image, uploads it to a public URL using UploadToURL, and publishes the final content to LinkedIn and Instagram.
